Mina: Heads-up — eu-west1 GNode pool saw a spike in GPU attach failures ~09:12 UTC. Noticed a correlated IOPS pressure on local SSDs.
Jason: link to the alert: https://alerts.internal/attaches/1716804321 
Mina: paste of iostat sample: ```Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await svctm %util
nvme0n1: 0.00 0.00 1.00 230.00 8.00 1840.00 16.00 1.20 5.10 0.18 41.00```
Xia: 230 w/s is tiny writes dominating — looks like lots of small fsyncs. overlayfs/cleanup + janitor sweeps?
ops-jen: Confirmed: janitor logs show many small deletes in /tmp and /scratch. Cleaner cadence overlapped with batch job spike.
Rafael: We saw similar last month but that was metadata-heavy scrub. This is different: write amplification from tiny write pattern (journaling + fsyncs).
Mina: Impact: attach latency > 12s causing k8s attach timeout -> pods stuck in Pending, autoscaler not compensating. Short-term mitigation idea: throttle janitor sweep, increase attach timeout, and enable prefix caching on hot hosts.
Jason: Can we try disabling fstrim/gc window temporarily on a small canary set? Risk: longer-term wear but avoids immediate attach fail.
Xia: Proposed quick actions: 
• 1) Pause janitor sweep for 10m on eu-west1 hot nodes (`/etc/ops/janitor.d/disable-euw-sweep`).
• 2) Deploy kernel io coalescing tweak via sysctl: `vm.dirty_bytes=134217728` and `vm.dirty_background_bytes=33554432` on canary set.
• 3) Increase k8s attach timeout from 30s -> 60s for pending jobs during rollback window.
ops-jen: I'll schedule the pause and sysctl on the 8 nodes with highest %util. tagging @oncall.
Rafael: Also add a temporary rewrite rule in the cleaner to batch deletes into fewer large ops (reduce tinywrites). Patch idea: switch cleaner to `--coalesce=enabled` for deletes.
deploy-bot: canary patch `cleaner-coalesce` deployed to eu-west1-canary at 1716804450 — monitoring metrics. :rocket:
Mina: After deploy, %util dropped to ~18% and attach latency fell to 3s. Still watching KV cache pressure.
Jason: Cost note — pushing longer buffers increases memory footprint on host. Ops OK with temporary bump? ops-jen: Approved for 2 hours, track memory + wear.
Xia: Next steps: run overnight sweep audit, add automated detection for tinywrite storms (threshold: >150 w/s and median write < 4KB). Create a dashboard panel.
Rafael: Long term: we should tune overlayfs writeback and consider collocating janitor windows away from batch launches. Also evaluate reconfiguring tempstore to coalesce small writes at the application layer.
Mina: Filing follow-up ticket: INFRA-1428 with root cause summary, mitigation steps, and rollback plan.
ops-jen: Note for oncall: if similar spike occurs, run `iostat -x 1 5` + `journalctl -u janitor | tail -n 200` and then tag this thread.
Jason: Thanks everyone. Good canary run. :thumbsup:
